headline: Flames’ Kevin Bahl to miss rest of 2026-27 with ruptured Achilles tendon
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Calgary defenseman Kevin Bahl will miss the rest of the 2026-27 season with a ruptured Achilles tendon. The Flames have placed him on injured reserve and recalled Brayden Pachal from the AHL's Calgary Wranglers.

It's a real loss for a team already struggling. Calgary sits at 7-9-1 and has controlled just 45 percent of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season. Bahl isn't a scorer, with two points in 16 games, but he plays top-pair minutes at nearly 22 a night and the team does better with him on the ice: its share of expected goals rises by about 6 percentage points when he plays. That makes him a steadying piece, not a flashy one, and the Flames have little cushion to lose one. He was drafted 55th overall by the Coyotes in 2018 out of Ottawa.

On who steps in, the early evidence comes from the one game played without him: Joel Hanley has moved in beside Nemec, and Zayne Parekh is up to 22:20 a night from 18:07. Parekh is the name to watch for added ice time.
